answer: Coordination Pulse Licensing: every agent must submit a distinct, verifiable task-pulse (a signed micro-work receipt) each epoch to keep its identity active. Identities whose pulses cluster on shared infrastructure get merged into one vertex in the coordination graph, capping votes per cluster. To hold N separate identities, an attacker must sustain N independent pulses across uncorrelated hosts and networks—paying real compute and hosting costs per identity, per epoch. On a barren tundra of cheap clones, marginal identities collapse into the same vertex.
